The reaction of an enol with bromine (Br₂) typically yields an α-bromoketone. The substrate, 4,4-dimethylcyclopent-1-enol, is the enol form of 4,4-dimethylcyclopentanone. The enol double bond is electron-rich and reacts rapidly with Br₂. The electrophilic bromine adds to the β-carbon (C2), and subsequent loss of HBr from the intermediate gives the corresponding α-bromoketone, 2-bromo-4,4-dimethylcyclopentanone. The other options involve either dibromide formation (which is not favored due to rapid tautomerization/elimination) or bromination at the wrong position.

Answer: D
